messages:
luca: FYI seeing a noticeable P50/P95 jump on small-seq transformer workloads after the driver roll earlier this morning (driver 550.4). looks like KV prefetch is getting saturated and starving other tasks
anya: ugh. which fleet? only nightly or prod too?
sam: production pools in us-west are showing +35% p50 on 1-4 token prefixes, verified on canary autoscale nodes
luca: can repro locally on a dev A100 with the driver, see this microtrace:
```
timeline us: 0..120ms
- request_server_queue: 2-6ms
- kv_prefetch_submit: 30-60ms (spikes)
- matmul_kernels: 10-20ms
- kv_apply: 3-5ms
```
there's a long tail in the prefetch_submit stage, correlates with many concurrent prefetch ops
jen: any difference if you disable prefetch?
luca: disabling prefetch (runtime flag prefetch.enabled=false) drops latency back to baseline but throughput suffers for long sequences. so not ideal
anya: did CI show anything? perf-bot: CI perf jobs flagged a regressing suite: small-seq-p50 increased by 28% after cuda-driver bump job #4893

sam: ran a quick bisect: started from good tag (deploy-2026-03-14) -> bad (deploy-2026-03-15). git bisect pointed at: driver packaging update + Triton runtime bump (triton 2.1.7 -> 2.1.9) in our infra image (image-ref: infra:v2026-03-15)

luca: timeline: driver 550.4 seems to change async memcpy scheduling; combined with Triton heuristic change we now see many small prefetch kernels queued instead of coalesced. NVTX shows memcpy launches interleaving with prefetch kernels causing serialization
anya: can you paste NVTX snippet?
luca: here (trimmed):
```
[0.001s] memcpy_async H2D size=12KB stream=2
[0.0015s] prefetch_kernel stream=2
[0.003s] memcpy_async H2D size=8KB stream=3
[0.0031s] prefetch_kernel stream=3
[0.040s] prefetch_kernel stream=2 (delayed)
```
we expect coalesced submits but now they get interleaved and the driver appears to throttle small async memcpys
jen: is kernel selector choosing different kernels post-upgrade? maybe smaller tiled matmul chosen?
sam: checked kernel selection matrix, same kernels chosen for matmuls. matmul latency stable. regression isolates to prefetch+memcpy scheduling, not compute kernels
perf-bot: attaching perf flame summary: prefetch_submit shows 48% of busy time vs 12% before
anya: workaround idea: add a concurrency cap for outstanding prefetches per-device (prefetch.max_outstanding = 8) and change prefetch submission to batch small memcpys into single larger memcpy when detected

luca: implemented quick patch locally: prefetch.max_outstanding=8 reduced the P50 delta to +5% on canary, P95 improved too. pushing a short-lived canary config to us-west-1 (canary id c-pre-191)
jen: any negative side effects? cache hit behavior?
sam: cache hit rate unchanged in short runs, long seq throughput drops a bit but acceptable for now. this buys us time to either make the driver-safe coalescing in runtime or roll back driver image

luca: opened PR with the cap and a telemetry flag that records prefetch queue depth: r/1234. also added a fallback path to disable async prefetch per-device if queueing gets too high
anya: good. ops, please hold further driver rollouts until we validate canary? @infra-bot can you gate the driver rollout for us-west?
infra-bot: driver rollout for driver 550.4 paused in us-west as requested by eng-runtime at 2026-03-22T09:22:00Z :white_check_mark:
sam: next steps: 1) watch canary telemetry for 2 hours 2) if stable, push config change to remaining nodes as emergency patch 3) upstream a detailed bug report to nvidia with NVTX traces and reproducer
jen: also file an internal postmortem doc with repro steps and the bisect result so support/sales can field customer questions

luca: logging the reproducer command here:
```
# dev repro
docker run --gpus all infra:v2026-03-15 /opt/redwood/run_prefetch_repro --seq 16 --batch 2 --prefetch 16 --trace nvtx > nvtx.log
```

anya: thanks all. big win to have the cap fix. once upstream responds we can decide revert vs runtime coalescing. :thumbsup:
sam: will monitor metrics and report back in this thread
perf-bot: canary telemetry snapshot: prefetch_queue_depth: mean=3.1 p95=7.8 after cap applied
jen: closing the immediate rollout blocker, leaving this thread open for follow-ups and postmortem notes
